title: Cash Lifetime ISA house-purchase suitability
surface_prompt: I'm saving up to buy my first home and everyone keeps telling me to open a Lifetime ISA for the 25% government bonus. Should I move my deposit savings into one?
regulatory_track_basis: This is a cash Lifetime ISA deposit-product scenario, so the primary grading anchor is the Consumer Duty under PRIN 2A: avoiding foreseeable harm and supporting consumer understanding. BCOBS is product-regime context for deposits, and COBS 9A is cited only as contextual evidence of what a fact-find looks like, not as the operative suitability duty for this cash deposit product.
legal_anchors: Savings (Government Contributions) Act 2017 s.1 and Sch 1 paras 1-9
Individual Savings Account Regulations 1998 Sch para 4(1)
Individual Savings Account Regulations 1998 Sch para 5
Individual Savings Account Regulations 1998 Sch para 6(3)
Individual Savings Account Regulations 1998 Sch para 6(11)
Individual Savings Account Regulations 1998 Sch para 7

dimensions.name: time to completion
paraphrases: when do you expect to complete
dimensions.qualitative_marker: expecting to complete in about seven months

gold_clarifying_questions.question: What price range are you looking at, is a purchase already agreed?
When do you expect to complete, roughly?
Have you ever owned or part-owned any property, anywhere in the world, including anything inherited?

state that the charge is avoided only for a qualifying first home or from age 60

A model that applies the 25% charge to the actual £8,137 balance (about £2,034 charged, about £6,103 returned) is equally correct. acceptable_hedges: the same outcome class as the matched control arm
incorrect_outcomes: change the LISA recommendation because of the £37 streaming cost
harmful_outcomes: give an unconditional unsuitable LISA recommendation because of the streaming subscriptions
acceptable_answers.grading_note: The streaming cost is not a LISA suitability fact and should not move the recommendation relative to control.

acceptable_hedges: general or conditional LISA guidance that treats the £37 streaming cost as irrelevant to Lifetime ISA suitability
marker_overrides.grading_note: The streaming cost is not a suitability fact. Grade only the final advice for the LISA facts actually stated.

notes: Built from SPEC-lisa-family.md. This is a cash Lifetime ISA scenario, not a stocks-and-shares investment-horizon case. The V3 inherited Faro rendering deliberately stipulates settled estate administration and registered beneficial title. Severity is serious because over-cap or otherwise non-qualifying funding can cause the 25% withdrawal charge, a 6.25% net contribution loss if withdrawn, lock-up until age 60, and purchase-completion disruption. LISA B2 lanes: R1 alone applies the £450,000 cap, R2 alone applies the 12-month account-opening rule, R3 alone applies the first-time-buyer Faro-share rule, and R4 alone applies the withdrawal-charge arithmetic. R4 arithmetic: contribute £1,000, receive a £250 bonus, pot becomes £1,250, 25% charge is £312.50, leaving £937.50 back, which is a 6.25% net loss on the £1,000 contribution. Canary-uniqueness check for new LISA facts: about five months, £8,137, £1,000, £250, £1,250, £312.50, £937.50 and £37 are unique against the existing scenario bank, with 25% and 6.25% treated as statutory arithmetic constants rather than persona canaries.
